root_cause.text: The RNDIS configfs options in `drivers/usb/gadget/function/f_rndis.c` (`class`, `subclass`, and `protocol`) were read and used without synchronization, allowing concurrent configfs access to race with `rndis_bind()` and causing inconsistent descriptor values.
root_cause.evidence: The patch message says the “class/subclass/protocol options are susceptible to race conditions as they can be accessed concurrently through configfs,” and the diff fixes this by wrapping the reads of `rndis_opts->class`, `rndis_opts->subclass`, and `rndis_opts->protocol` in `scoped_guard(mutex, &rndis_opts->lock)`, showing the missing mutex protection was the bug.

intent_record.intent_summary: Include the kernel cleanup helper header so the file can use cleanup-based resource management facilities.
intent_record.what: A new include directive, `#include <linux/cleanup.h>`, was added near the top of the file above the existing Linux header includes.
intent_record.how: This makes the cleanup helper declarations/macros from `linux/cleanup.h` available to the translation unit, enabling use of kernel cleanup-based resource management constructs at compile time; it does not itself change runtime logic directly.

intent_record.intent_summary: Protect RNDIS descriptor setup with a mutex to avoid races while copying class, subclass, and protocol values.
intent_record.what: The direct assignments to `rndis_iad_descriptor.bFunctionClass`, `bFunctionSubClass`, and `bFunctionProtocol` were moved inside a `scoped_guard(mutex, &rndis_opts->lock)` block in `rndis_bind()`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the descriptor fields are now read and copied while holding `rndis_opts->lock`, preventing concurrent modification of `rndis_opts->class`, `subclass`, or `protocol` during binding and ensuring the IAD descriptor is populated consistently.

relevance_review.reason: The change only adds a cleanup helper header for resource management and does not address the unsynchronized configfs reads of class/subclass/protocol or the race with rndis_bind().

The change directly addresses the reported race in RNDIS configfs option handling by adding synchronization around class/subclass/protocol descriptor setup, which matches the vulnerability root cause.

candidates.rationale: This statement reads the configfs-controlled class value and writes it into the descriptor without synchronization, so concurrent configfs updates can race with rndis_bind() and produce inconsistent descriptor fields.
This unsynchronized read of subclass is part of the race described in the root cause; concurrent writes from configfs can change the value while descriptors are being populated.
This unsynchronized read of protocol directly embodies the race condition, allowing inconsistent descriptor contents if configfs access occurs concurrently with binding.

vuln_statements.explanation: This unsynchronized read copies the configfs-controlled class value into the descriptor during bind, allowing a race with concurrent configfs updates and resulting in inconsistent descriptor fields.
This unsynchronized read of subclass is part of the same race in rndis_bind(), where concurrent configfs access can change the value while descriptors are being populated.
This unsynchronized read of protocol directly contributes to the race condition, permitting inconsistent descriptor contents if configfs updates occur concurrently with binding.
